label: Caprock Mesa: repeated part_replaced on module with declining benefit
headline: Twenty-five modules at Caprock Mesa have been broken across four separate mower rock-strike incidents because contractually specified mower deck deflectors were never fitted — a preventable, recurring loss with an open technician recommendation unactioned since September 2024.
action: Issue a vegetation-management corrective action requiring the mow contractor to fit the site-specified deck deflectors and evidence compliance before the next mow cycle, and close out the open recommendation from WO-2024-00175.
reasoning: H2 is correct about the metric — benefit_pct is null on all five members, so the 'declining benefit' trend has no quantitative basis and the 0.33 late-ineffective share is one WO (WO-2024-00175) coded ESCALATED because the tech asked for a process fix — but the cluster still surfaced a real, repeating, preventable loss mechanism. Three different technicians (TECH-0072, TECH-0117, TECH-0044) independently attribute the breakage to rock thrown off the mower deck (WO-2024-00172, WO-2024-00175, WO-2024-00237, WO-2025-00220), and WO-2024-00175 gives the discriminating physical signature H1 predicts: impact points on the lower third with glass starred outward, plus the statement that this is the fourth such incident and that specified deck deflectors were never fitted. H3 fails because the matched controls contain no storm, hail or wind damage on any component in the Sep–Oct 2024 window — the only other Caprock Mesa module work is soiling washes, clamp torque checks and IR flights (WO-2025-00238, WO-2025-00072, WO-2026-00177), all routine and unremarkable. H4 is right that WO-2024-00045 is a separate EL-driven warranty return population in B02 and should be excluded, but removing it still leaves four impact events, 25 modules and a repeat hit on B04 (WO-2024-00175, WO-2025-00220), which is a pattern, not ordinary variation. The open corrective recommendation has been sitting unactioned since 2024-09-23 and B04 was broken again six months later.
contradicting: The candidate's stated signal (efficacy decay) is not real — all five members have null benefit_pct and every impact WO reports string current verified back to normal after replacement, so the replacements themselves are effective. WO-2024-00045 belongs to an unrelated EL/warranty population and inflates the cluster to n=5. No deflector-fitting or vegetation-management corrective WO appears in the data, so the counterfactual (damage stops after the fix) is untested, and the 2025-03-17 event falls outside typical peak mow season.

population_detail.description: Modules destroyed by mower-thrown rock in four documented incidents across B04, B06 and B08 (1 + 7 + 12 + 5), with B04 hit twice. The forward-exposed population is the lowest module row along every mow lane at Caprock Mesa, which cannot be sized without installed-base data.
population_detail.basis: Counted directly from module quantities stated in the narratives of WO-2024-00172, WO-2024-00175, WO-2024-00237 and WO-2025-00220; the 13 modules in WO-2024-00045 are excluded as a separate EL warranty return.

hypotheses.statement: The module replacements at Caprock Mesa are driven by a repeatable ground-maintenance process defect — mowing without the specified deck deflectors throwing rock into the lower module edge — not by any module or replacement-part failure mode.
predictions: Narratives for the impact-related WOs consistently describe damage on the lower third / bottom row of cells with outward-starred glass, and name the mower or rock strike as the cause
Damage events cluster in the growing/mowing season and in blocks adjacent to mow lanes or drivable row ends, with the same blocks (e.g. B04) recurring
At least one prior WO exists referencing earlier incidents of the same kind ('fourth incident'), i.e. three or more antecedent mower-damage WOs at this site before 2024-09-23
Replacement outcomes are coded 'resolved' with string current verified normal — recurrence is at the site/block level, not at the replaced-module level
If a deflector-fitting or vegetation-management corrective WO is ever logged, module glass-damage WOs at this site fall to near zero afterwards
discriminating_evidence: Damage location described as lower-third/edge impact (mower) versus distributed or upper-surface damage (hail)
Presence of an open corrective action or recommendation about mower deflectors that has never been closed out
Repeat damage in the same blocks over multiple mowing cycles rather than one date cluster

hypotheses.statement: The 'declining benefit' signal is a metric artifact: benefit_pct is null for all five members, so the efficacy trend is computed purely from coarse outcome/uncertainty flags, and the 0.33 late-ineffective share is a single WO out of three.
predictions: mean_benefit_early_pct, mean_benefit_late_pct and benefit_drop_pct are all null for this cluster, i.e. no quantitative efficacy was ever measured
The one 'ineffective' late member is WO-2024-00175, flagged recurring/escalated because the technician recommended a process fix, not because the replacement failed
All other members carry outcome 'resolved' with narrative confirmation that string current returned to normal or within tolerance
Recomputing the cluster with the two 'uncertain:true' records excluded, or with any single record removed, changes the late-ineffective share by 33 percentage points or more
Other clusters at other sites with n<=6 and all-null benefit_pct show similarly volatile early/late ineffective shares
discriminating_evidence: Whether any member has a non-null benefit_pct at all; if none do, the decay claim has no quantitative basis
Sensitivity test: leave-one-out recomputation of early/late shares
Whether 'recurring' in the extracted fields is triggered by phrases about site-level repeat incidents rather than by the same asset returning to failure

hypotheses.statement: The September–October 2024 breakages across B04, B06 and B08 are the aftermath of one or two discrete hail/wind events, with technicians defaulting to the familiar 'rock strike' attribution.
predictions: Module glass-damage WOs across multiple non-adjacent blocks are opened within a narrow window (2024-09-21 to 2024-10-24) after a long quiet period
Other component types (trackers, combiner enclosures, met station, fencing) show damage or inspection WOs in the same window
Damage counts scale with block area rather than with mow-lane adjacency
Environment fields or narratives elsewhere in that window mention storm, hail, wind or debris
No comparable module-damage WOs occur in months with equivalent mowing activity but no storms
discriminating_evidence: Presence or absence of same-window damage WOs on non-module components
Whether damaged modules within a block are spread across all rows/heights (hail) or concentrated in the lowest module row nearest ground level (mower)
Whether the 2025-03-17 event (outside typical mow season) matches the same signature

hypotheses.statement: The cluster is a merge of two unrelated populations — one EL-driven warranty return campaign and several mechanical impact repairs — so its size and any apparent trend are ordinary variation for a site of this installed base.
predictions: WO-2024-00045 is wo_type Warranty with resolution VENDOR-REFERRED and symptom 'other', driven by EL imagery, while the remaining four are CM with impact symptoms — two distinct causal chains sharing only action='part_replaced'
Excluding the warranty WO leaves n=4, too few to support an early/late split
Modules replaced per MW per year at Caprock Mesa is comparable to other sites in the corpus once warranty-campaign removals are separated from impact damage
Total labor of 23.3 h for ~38 modules is consistent with routine swap rates elsewhere in the corpus, indicating no escalating repair difficulty
Similar site|part_replaced|module clusters exist at other sites with comparable n and no flagged decay
discriminating_evidence: Cross-site normalisation of module replacements per MW (or per installed module count) per year
Whether the warranty campaign WO shares any block, tech, symptom or failure signature with the impact WOs
Whether the corpus contains other sites with n=5 module-replacement clusters that were not flagged, implying selection on noise

exposure_note: Priced at the cost model's inverter replacement rate. This population is not inverters, so treat the count as the reliable figure and this dollar value as indicative only.
